_about: Hand corrections applied by scripts/build_dataset.py to items parsed from the printed editions. 'match' is text found in the printed heading. Each correction says why.

items.match: SEMICENTENNIAL CELEBRATION OF THE FOUNDING OF AGRICULTURAL COLLEGES
items.title: The Man Who Works with His Hands
items.occasion: Semicentennial of the founding of agricultural colleges in the United States, Michigan Agricultural College
items.why: The machine-read heading lost the month and day; Day by Day places the college address on May 31, 1907.
A photograph caption read as text, not an address.

_about_trc: Corrections to Theodore Roosevelt Center catalog records, keyed by TRC record id, made from reading the document itself. keep_id keeps the speech's id stable.

trc.title: Remarks at South Vernon, Massachusetts
trc.note: The catalog record says Mount Vernon; the typed heading of the document reads South Vernon, Mass.
trc.why: Typed heading on LOC reel 424 frame 0607 reads 'SOUTH VERNON, MASS.'; both transcription passes agree.

trc.title: Reply to a delegation of the Merchants' Association of New York
trc.note: A press account: William F. King, chairman of the delegation, speaks first; the President's reply follows.
trc.why: The catalog title names King's address, but the document (LOC reel 424 frame 0460) also gives Roosevelt's reply, which is why it is in this collection.

trc.note: This is the extract given to the press. The full address, headed "Address of President Roosevelt at Fitchburg, Mass., Sept. 2, 1902," is on the pages just before it (LOC reel 424, frames 0619 to 0622) and is not yet transcribed here.
trc.why: The catalog record gives only September 1902; the full address on the preceding folios is headed Sept. 2, 1902, as read by the second transcriber.

trc.title: A Talk with Comrades, Spanish War Veterans, Detroit
trc.note: The document is printed pages cut into slips, not a typescript. It is a longer text of the Detroit address to the Spanish War Veterans than the one printed in Presidential Addresses and State Papers, which is listed separately.
trc.why: Both transcription passes read the opening 'Mr. Mayor, and Men and Women of Michigan, and particularly you, My Comrades, who volunteered in the war with Spain'; the 1910 printed text of the same evening differs and is about a quarter of the length.

trc.title: The Industrial Problems, Wheeling
trc.note: The document is pages 29 to 34 of a printed pamphlet pasted into the volume, not a typescript. Its text of the Wheeling address is longer than the one printed in Presidential Addresses and State Papers, which is listed separately.
trc.why: Both transcription passes read the typed heading 'Speech of the President at Wheeling, W. Va., September 6, 1902'; the pamphlet text runs about 3,600 words against about 2,600 in the 1910 volume.
Address of Secretary of War Elihu Root at Junction City, Kansas, May 2, 1903 - not a speech by Roosevelt (catalog title).
